activities.title: Write your Lab 4 key message
activities.intro: Write one sentence that people should remember from your Lab 4 deck. Write it on paper first, then type it here.

items: Fill in the blanks: "After this course, I can [a skill], which helps me [a task at work or at home]."
Write your sentence on your paper first.
Type it below, then paste it in the chat too.
Keep it. It becomes the title or the closing line of your Lab 4 deck.

blocks.prompt: Your key message in one sentence
Which one is a strong key message?
options: I learned many things about computers.
After this course, I can build a spreadsheet with formulas, which helps me total our office supplies in seconds.

blocks.prompt: Your section chief hears only one sentence from your briefing. Which planning question does that sentence answer?

help: Is it specific? Name the skill, not just "computers".
Does it say so what? Add the task it helps you do, at work or at home.

activities.title: Read the 5-box storyboard
activities.intro: Look at the example storyboard for "My Digital Skills Journey" on the screen. Each box is one slide with one idea. Match each box to its job.

items: Look at the five boxes on the screen.
Notice that each box has one idea and a title that says something.
Match each box below to its job: title, hook, proof or close.

blocks.prompt: What job does each box do?
items: Name, date, one photo
"I typed letters twice because I didn't save."
Lab 2: 3 letters in one click
The Lab 3 chart
Key message + next step

blocks.prompt: How many boxes (slides) meet the Lab 4 minimum?

activities.title: Storyboard your Lab 4 deck on paper
activities.intro: Paper and pen, no computer. Sketch your Lab 4 deck one box per slide, then show your paper to the camera. You may storyboard "Our Office Supplies Inventory" or a community project pitch instead.

items: Write your key message at the top of the page.
Draw 5 or 6 boxes (fold the paper in half, then in thirds).
In each box: a title that says something and a rough sketch (chart, photo, icon).
Mark where your Lab 3 chart or Lab 1 image goes.
Number the boxes in the order you'll present them.

blocks.prompt: Which slide title says something, not just a label?
In the example storyboard, which box holds the Lab 3 chart?
A photo of your paper storyboard

help: Rough is fine: stick figures and wavy lines for text.
A title like "Module 3" is only a label. Ask: what did Module 3 let me do?
Finished early? Write a one-line note under each box: what you will say, not what you'll write on the slide.

activities.title: Spot the problems on a bad slide
activities.intro: Look at the "MY DIGITAL SKILLS JOURNEY!!!" slide on the screen. Find at least five problems, using the design words: contrast, alignment, repetition, proximity, readability.

blocks.prompt: Which principle does each problem break?
items: Yellow text on a purple gradient
A wall of small text
Three fonts, ALL CAPS and "!!!"
No key message: it's a list of topics

blocks.prompt: Nothing lines up and the text floats mid-slide. Which principle is that?

activities.title: Quick check: what to decide first

blocks.prompt: You must brief your section chief on the supplies inventory in 5 minutes. What do you decide first?
options: The one key message and what you need from the chief
